Kiosk app version in the heartbeat + on shed start (from 2026-03-11 steward sync; Maya/Teo/Ana ask). Constraint: NO desk changes. "Heartbeat" = the kiosk's GET /sync/pulse poll every PULSE_INTERVAL (15s); it's what shows in the desk logs (the desk proxy writes every request as JSON to logs/access.log incl. request.uri and ALL request headers — verified on the test desk: User-Agent "Python/3.11 httpx/0.27", X-Kiosk-Key). Today a running kiosk can't know its version: make pack-app bundles only src/{kiosk,loans,labels,scanner}; setup.toml isn't in the bundle and the makefile's Version file is written outside the bundled dirs. Plan (kiosk only): (1) pack-app writes kiosk/VERSION (version + build date) into the bundle, with a small reader that falls back to "unknown"; (2) add header `X-Kiosk-Version: <version>` to every desk request through ONE shared helper next to the version reader (e.g. `kiosk_headers()`) that every call site uses, so no path can miss it now or later. Call sites (all five): PulseClient httpx incl. the /sync/pulse poll (src/kiosk/poller.py `_headers`), RelayClient requests (src/kiosk/relay_client.py `self.headers`), the authenticated curl in poller.py (`--header "X-Kiosk-Key: ..."`), the legacy old-route curl in poller.py (currently no `--header` on purpose to keep the token off argv — add only the version header, never the token, and update its "No --header" comment), and the outbox loan uploads in src/kiosk/report_sender.py (`_build_headers()`, sent via `requests.post`) — keep User-Agent unchanged; the proxy logs it next to every heartbeat, desk ignores unknown headers; absence = pre-2.4.1 kiosk. Open check: confirm the log index keeps request headers (search the index for "httpx"); fallback is a query param `/sync/pulse?v=<version>` which always appears in the logged uri. Side finding for Ana (desk-side, not this task): access.log stores the full X-Kiosk-Key token for every kiosk request — the proxy should redact that header. Unused alternative considered: post_status()/POST /sync/status exists but is never called and nothing on the desk displays it.
